text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Deputy prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas refused a personal security guard appointed by Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius last week.
- The membership of NATO is a very realistic thing now, said parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis.
- Prime minister Gediminas Vagnorius appointed Romas Kilikauskas, 61, the vice minister of interior affairs. Kilikauskas served in the U.S. aviation intelligence until 1992.

- Preliminary financial results of commercial banks show that Vilnius Bank led in terms of growth but Hermis Bank was highest in terms of net profit. Reliable information will be available only after shareholders meetings at the end of March.
- Inflation in Lithuania went down in February to 0.6 percent, the statistics department said.

- President Algirdas Brazauskas said on Saturday that he will form the country's official foreign policy and stressed that Lithuanian security and stability could be ensured only by full membership in NATO.

- Parliament starts its spring session today. Major attention during the session will be paid to legislation, economic and social matters. According to the Constitution, the spring session is to continue untill June 30.
- Finnish Lahden Poltimo decided to invest some $3 million into the reconstruction of the Kalnapilis malt factory and to supply the whole country with locally-produced malt.
- Dirbtinis Pluoshtas shares should go up since according to unaudited results its net profit in 1996 increased by 15.9 percent.

- Baltic countries joined Reuters. The newspaper publishes an interview with chief correspondent of Nordic and Baltic countries Simon Haydon about the launch of Reuters Baltic News in the country on March 13.
- The foreign trade deficit is 4.3 billion litas and officials expect to reduce it with the help of the government's export encouragement fund.
